# Adjudication Task — Chapter 565

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃565화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|매직 존슨이 떠난 뒤, 연락을 받지 않는 최 팀장에게 문자를 남긴 나는 곧장 길드 하우스 최상층에 마련된 개인 사무실로 향했다.
  6|
  7|쾅.
  8|
  9|등 뒤로 거칠게 문이 닫히는 소리를 들으며 바닥에 털썩 주저앉았다.
 10|
 11|자그마한 책상과 의자 하나가 전부인 백여 평의 공간.
 12|
 13|사무실이라 쓰고 연무장(鍊武場)이라 읽는 그곳에서 나는 즉시 스마트폰을 꺼내 칩을 밀어 넣었다.
 14|
 15|달칵.
 16|
 17|얼마 전에 바꾼 최신형 스마트폰에는 없는 기능이 없었다.
 18|
 19|십여 년 전부터 보편화되기 시작한 홀로그램 영상 재생 기능도 그중 하나였다.
 20|
 21|지이잉.
 22|
 23|미세한 소음과 함께 스마트폰에 장착된 재생기에서 빛이 흘러나온다.
 24|
 25|한발 빠르게 허공섭물(虛空攝物)의 수법으로 폐쇄형 커튼을 친 나는 어두운 사무실 내부를 가득 채우기 시작한 홀로그램 영상에 집중했다.
 26|
 27|- 치직. 치지직.
 28|
 29|노이즈.
 30|
 31|- 퍼벙, 콰아아앙!
 32|
 33|굉음.
 34|
 35|- 취리리리릭!
 36|
 37|몬스터의 울음소리와.
 38|
 39|- 으아아악!
 40|
 41|인간의 비명.
 42|
 43|그 모든 것들이 눈앞에서 뒤섞이고, 흩어진다. 크고 작은 텐트와 건물이 늘어선 그곳은 어느덧 참혹한 전쟁터로 돌변해 있었다.
 44|
 45|‘변이 게이트.’
 46|
 47|자연스럽게 그 다섯 글자가 머릿속을 스친 그때.
 48|
 49|- 알라의 이름으로!
 50|
 51|- 와아아아!
 52|
 53|군용 모자와 터번을 뒤집어쓴 일단의 무리가 악에 받힌 고함과 함께 나아간다.
 54|
 55|아랍계로 짐작되는 그들의 전신은 누군가의 붉은 피로 흠뻑 젖었다.
 56|
 57|그중에는 기껏해야 초등학생쯤으로 보이는 어린아이까지 포함되어 있었다.
 58|
 59|‘어린아이라니…….’
 60|
 61|이런 자들이 정규군일 리가 없다.
 62|
 63|통일되지 않고 뒤죽박죽인 복장을 봤을 때부터 짐작했던 사실이지만, 그들은 대격변이 시작되기 전부터 중동을 피로 물들인 아랍 반군이 분명했다.
 64|
 65|그리고 다음 순간.
 66|
 67|- 으아아! 시, 신은 위대하시다!
 68|
 69|공포에 질린 꼬마의 외침과 함께, 저마다의 손에 들린 수많은 화기가 불을 뿜었다.
 70|
 71|타탕! 투다다다다!
 72|
 73|슈우욱, 퍼엉!
 74|
 75|평범한 인간이었다면 벌집이 되었을 화력이 단숨에 퍼부어진다. 하지만 그들이 상대하는 적들은 평범하지도 않았고, 인간도 아니었다.
 76|
 77|콰아아아!
 78|
 79|폭발과 동시에 거대한 화염이 솟구친다.
 80|
 81|사방을 가득 채운 검은 연기를 보며 반군들이 거친 숨을 몰아쉬던 그때, 연기가 좌우로 갈라지며 섬광이 번뜩였다.
 82|
 83|쉭, 서걱!
 84|
 85|단 일격이면 족했다. 반월의 형태로 뻗어나간 검붉은 마력은 막아서는 모든 것을 절단했다.
 86|
 87|목, 허리, 가슴. 저마다의 차이는 있었지만, 그 결과는 같았다.
 88|
 89|죽음.
 90|
 91|촤아아악!
 92|
 93|한 박자 늦게 뿜어져 나온 피분수가 모래를 붉게 물들인다.
 94|
 95|스물에 달하는 동료들의 처참한 최후를 눈앞에서 목격한 반군들이 눈을 부릅떴다.
 96|
 97|- 마, 마수드!
 98|
 99|- 신이시여…….
100|
101|그러나 그들의 신은 모습을 드러내지도, 신도들의 목소리에 응답하지도 않았다.
102|
103|신을 대신하여 나타난 것은 녹색 피갑을 전신에 두른 괴물이었다.
104|
105|- 치륵. 치리리릭.
106|
107|세모꼴의 머리와 파르르 진동하는 두 개의 더듬이. 낫처럼 구부러진 앞다리를 지닌 괴물의 정체는 사마귀였다.
108|
109|놈은 성인 남성을 내려다볼 만큼 거대했고, 강한 마력을 띤 몸뚱어리에는 앞서 반군들이 퍼부은 화력에도 흠집 하나 없었다.
110|
111|- 자, 자이언트 맨티스(Giant Mantis)…….
112|
113|누군가가 신음처럼 중얼거린 그 순간, 거대한 앞다리가 다시 한번 허공을 내리그었다.
114|
115|후웅, 서걱!
116|
117|멍하니 얼어붙어 있던 반군의 몸뚱어리가 좌우로 쪼개진다. 앞다리에 실린 마력이 화살처럼 날아가 사방을 찢어발겼다.
118|
119|서걱! 서걱! 콰아아앙!
120|
121|인간. 무기. 심지어는 황급히 출동시킨 전차마저 마력을 막아서지 못했다.
122|
123|사방을 베고 가르는 공격에 폭발음과 비명이 연이어 울려 퍼지고, 어느새 다섯 마리로 늘어난 자이언트 맨티스는 인간들을 향해 뛰어들었다.
124|
125|- 치치치칫!
126|
127|- 치리이잇!
128|
129|퍼석! 촤아악!
130|
131|기묘한 울음소리가 흘러나올 때마다 백여 명에 달하는 반군들의 사지가 날아가고 피가 튀었다.
132|
133|신을 부르짖으며 발악하던 자도, 공포에 질려 도망치던 자도 사막에 쓰러져 두 번 다시 일어나지 못했다.
134|
135|- 으아, 으아아아!
136|
137|푸욱!
138|
139|낫 같은 앞다리가 등을 가르고 가슴뼈를 부수었다.
140|
141|마지막으로 저항하던 반군의 등에 일격을 꽂아 넣은 자이언트 맨티스가 문득 돌아섰다.
142|
143|얼굴 옆으로 툭 튀어나온 붉은 눈동자가 정확히 화면을 응시한다.
144|
145|‘카메라를 발견했어.’
146|
147|놈은 카메라를 봤고, 나는 놈을 봤다.
148|
149|그리고 이상함을 느낀 자이언트 맨티스가 조심스럽게 카메라를 향해 다가오던 그 순간.
150|
151|- 신의 불꽃이 이곳에 임할지니. 파이어 레인(Fire Rain)!
152|
153|화악!
154|
155|누군가의 창노한 외침. 동시에 마나로 형성된 불덩이 수십여 개가 자이언트 맨티스의 어깨너머로 유성처럼 쏟아졌다.
156|
157|- 치리리리릿!
158|
159|기성(奇聲)을 토한 자이언트 맨티스가 불덩이를 향해 자신의 앞발을 휘둘렀다.
160|
161|꽈앙!
162|
163|격돌과 함께 화면이, 아니 온 사방이 붉게 물들고. 저 멀리에서 나타난 수십여 명의 헌터가 터져 나가는 불덩이를 뚫고 전장을 질주했다.
164|
165|- 알라후 아크바르으!
166|
167|- 신은 위대하시다! 저 악마들을 모조리 죽여라!
168|
169|- 크륵, 취잇!
170|
171|인간과 몬스터. 몬스터와 인간.
172|
173|두 종족은 또 다시 죽고 죽이는 싸움을 시작했다. 그러나 나는 극으로 치닫는 이 전투의 결과를 끝까지 지켜볼 수 없었다.
174|
175|치직. 치지지직. 팟!
176|
177|그야말로 찰나의 순간이었다.
178|
179|극심한 노이즈와 함께 방안을 가득 채우고 있던 홀로그램 영상이 씻은 듯이 사라진 것은.
180|
181|“……후.”
182|
183|참았던 숨을 뱉어낸 나는 잠시 내려놓았던 스마트폰을 집어 들었다.
184|
185|칩 안에 내장된 목록을 확인해 보니 남은 영상이 스무 개가 넘는다.
186|
187|‘시벌, 지난번에 영상 받은 지 얼마나 됐다고 또.’
188|
189|전년도 대비 마력 수치 7% 상승.
190|
191|어느 멍청한 놈들은 ‘고작’이라고 생각할 만한 수치일지도 모르겠다.
192|
193|하지만 산소 농도가 몇 퍼센트라도 하락하면 난리가 나듯이, 이건 상황이 개판으로 돌아가고 있다는 증거였다.
194|
195|아니, 어쩌면…….
196|
197|‘두 번째 대격변의 시작일지도 모르지.’
198|
199|그리고 남은 영상들을 차례차례 확인할수록, 마음에 품고 있는 불안감은 점차 실체를 지니기 시작했다.
200|
201|‘유럽. 중동, 서아프리카. 동남아시아…… 무슨 세계 대축제도 아니고.’
202|
203|이미 전 세계 곳곳에서 동시다발적으로 변화가 일어나고 있었다.
204|
205|파트라슈가 개껌 물고 뛰어다닐 것 같은 스위스의 푸른 언덕에 신규 게이트가 생성되고, 반군과 정규군이 서로를 향해 포탄을 퍼붓는 동안 방치된 하급 게이트에서는 몬스터들이 쏟아져 나온다.
206|
207|몇몇 영상에서는 방비가 철저했는지 조기 진압에 성공하기도 했지만, 과반수 이상의 경우에는 상당한 피해를 입은 뒤에야 몬스터를 물리칠 수 있었다.
208|
209|‘이건.’
210|
211|영상을 계속해서 돌려보던 나는 문득 미간을 좁혔다.
212|
213|이와 같은 피해가 단순히 게이트의 방비가 부족했기 때문만이 아니라는 것을 알아차렸기 때문이었다.
214|
215|그리고 그 순간 찾아온 것은 깨달음뿐만이 아니었다.
216|
217|띵.
218|
219|귓가를 파고드는 엘리베이터의 미세한 소음과 함께, 서서히 가까워지는 두 사람의 인기척.
220|
221|초대하지 않은 불청객들의 정체를 알아차린 나는 손을 뻗었다.
222|
223|화악.
224|
225|따스한 바람이 불었다.
226|
227|손바닥을 타고 흘러나온 기운이 부드럽게 문을 밀어젖히자, 익숙한 얼굴들이 시야에 들어왔다.
228|
229|“이제 오면 어떡합니까. 문자 보낸 지가 언젠데.”
230|
231|“죄송합니다. 잠시 연락이 불가능한 상황이었던 터라.”
232|
233|지각생을 갈구려던 나는 고개를 갸웃거렸다.
234|
235|“연락이 불가능한 상황? 게이트라도 다녀왔어요?”
236|
237|“음, 비슷합니다.”
238|
239|“……맞으면 맞고, 아니면 아닌 거지 비슷한 건 또 뭐야.”
240|
241|“김 집사님과 잠깐 들를 곳이 있었습니다. 중요한 볼일이라 어쩔 수 없었죠.”
242|
243|매끄럽게 대답한 최 팀장이 안으로 걸음을 내디뎠다. 자연스럽게 뒤를 따라 들어온 김 집사가 문을 닫으며 가벼운 눈인사를 건넨다.
244|
245|‘저 양반도 오랜만이네.’
246|
247|길드에도 통 얼굴을 안 비추던 김 집사와 중요한 볼일이라. 뭘까?
248|
249|약 일주일 만에 보는 얼굴과 함께 일말의 의문이 남았지만, 지금은 그보다 더 급한 일이 기다리고 있다.
250|
251|그 사실을 모를 리 없는 최 팀장이 먼저 입을 열었다.
252|
253|“이 이야기는 뒤로 미루고, 우선 미스터 존슨이 줬다는 정보부터 확인해 봐야겠군요.”
254|
255|“아, 여기요.”
256|
257|다시 한번 홀로그램 영상이 흘러나오고 얼마나 시간이 흘렀을까.
258|
259|모든 영상과 첨부된 자료를 확인한 두 사람의 표정은 딱딱하게 굳어져 있었다.
260|
261|“전 세계 마력 수치 7% 상승?”
262|
263|언제나 부드럽던 목소리가 갈라져 나온다. 신음처럼 중얼거린 김 집사가 최 팀장을 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
264|
265|“도련님.”
266|
267|“예. 짐작했던 것 이상으로 진행 상황이 빠릅니다. 상황이 심각해요.”
268|
269|7%면 상승이 아니라, 폭등(暴騰)이라고 부르는 것이 더 어울린다.
270|
271|그리고 이러한 마력 수치의 급격한 변화는 영상 속에서 특히 두드러졌다.
272|
273|“몬스터들이…….”
274|
275|고개를 끄덕인 내가 최 팀장의 말을 받았다.
276|
277|“예. 존나게 쎄졌어요.”
278|
279|마력 수치의 상승은, 곧 몬스터의 힘이 강력해진다는 것을 의미한다.
280|
281|첫 영상에서 자이언트 맨티스가 파이어 레인을 맞고도 그럭저럭 싸우는 것만 봐도 알 수 있는 사실이다.
282|
283|‘치코리타가 리자몽 불꽃으로 선탠하는 꼴이지.’
284|
285|엄연히 상성이라는 것이 존재하는 법인데, 상승한 마력 수치와 더불어 강해진 몬스터들은 그 상성을 조금씩 무시하고 있었다.
286|
287|이런 개 같은 상황이니, 만일을 대비하여 헌터라는 귀한 인력을 최소한으로 운용하던 곳은 속수무책으로 무너질 수밖에.
288|
289|지금 상황을 요약하자면 한마디로…….
290|
291|“좆 됐습니다. 지금 개판 오 분 전이에요.”
292|
293|미쳐 버린 진행 속도다. 이대로라면 당장 올해 연말쯤에는 일기 예보에 몬스터가 등장할지도 모른다.
294|

“…”

Monsters raining down from the sky.

Team Leader Choi definitely stuck to what was right.

[P186]

“Yes?”

[P193]
“I said that I would make Gate defenses my top priority. I never said I would put matters concerning Ares Guild on hold.”

[P194]
“…”

*What?*

“Then that important errand was…?”

[P201]
“Everything crumbles from the inside.”

[P51]
Someone groaned the name. The huge foreleg swept through the air again.

[P52]
*Whoom. Shing!*

[P53]
A rebel frozen in place split down the middle. Magical power shot from the foreleg like an arrow, tearing through everything around it.

[P54]
*Shing! Shing! Kraaang!*

[P55]
People. Weapons. Even the tanks hastily sent into battle could not stop it.

[P56]
Explosions and screams rang out as the attacks cut in every direction. Before long, there were five Giant Mantises, and they leaped among the humans.

[P57]
*Chit-chit-chit!*

[P58]
*Chiriiit!*

[P59]
*Crack! Splaaash!*

[P60]
With every strange cry, limbs flew from the roughly hundred rebels, and blood sprayed across the sand.

[P61]
Those who fought while calling on their god and those who fled in terror alike fell in the desert, never to rise again.

[P62]
“Aaah! Aaaaah!”

[P63]
*Shunk!*

[P64]
A scythe-like foreleg sliced into a rebel’s back and shattered his breastbone.

[P65]
Having struck down the last rebel still resisting, the Giant Mantis suddenly turned. A red eye protruding from the side of its head fixed on the camera.

[P66]
*It found the camera.*

[P67]
It saw the camera, and I saw it.

[P68]
The Giant Mantis seemed to sense something strange. It began to approach cautiously—

[P69]
“May the flames of God descend upon this place. Fire Rain!”

[P70]
*Fwoosh!*

[P71]
An aged voice rang out. At the same instant, dozens of fireballs formed from mana came hurtling over the Giant Mantis’s shoulder like meteors.

[P72]
*Chiririririt!*

[P73]
It shrieked and swung a foreleg at them.

[P74]
*Boom!*

[P75]
The impact dyed the screen—no, everything around it—red. Dozens of Hunters appeared in the distance and raced across the battlefield through the bursting fireballs.

[P76]
“Allahu Akbar!”

[P77]
“God is great! Kill every one of those devils!”

[P78]
*Krrk, chiiit!*

[P79]
Humans and monsters. Monsters and humans.

[P80]
The two sides began killing each other again. But I couldn’t watch the battle to its end.

[P81]
*Crackle. Crackle. Pop!*

[P82]
In an instant, the hologram filling the room vanished amid a burst of heavy static.

[P83]
“…Whew.”

[P84]
I let out the breath I’d been holding and picked up the phone I’d set aside. The list on the chip held more than twenty videos I hadn’t watched yet.

[P85]
*Fuck. How long has it been since the last batch? And there’s already more.*

[P86]
Worldwide magical power readings had risen seven percent over the previous year.

[P87]
Some idiots might call that *only* seven percent. But a drop of even a few percentage points in the air’s oxygen concentration would cause an uproar. This was proof that things were going to hell.

[P88]
No. Maybe…

[P89]
*This could be the beginning of a second Great Cataclysm.*

[P90]
As I watched the remaining videos one by one, my fears began to take shape.

[P91]
*Europe. The Middle East. West Africa. Southeast Asia… What is this, some kind of worldwide festival?*

[P92]
Changes were already happening all over the world at once.

[P93]
A new Gate appeared among the green hills of Switzerland, where I could picture Patrache running around with a dog biscuit in his mouth.[^2] Elsewhere, rebels and regular soldiers rained shells on each other while monsters poured from low-rank Gates left unattended.

[P94]
A few places had been prepared well enough to suppress the outbreaks early. In more than half the videos, though, the monsters were defeated only after causing considerable damage.

[P95]
*Wait.*

[P96]
I kept replaying the footage, my brow furrowing. The damage wasn’t simply due to poor Gate defenses.

[P97]
But insight wasn’t the only thing that came to me then.

[P98]
*Ding.*

[P99]
I heard the faint chime of the elevator, followed by the presence of two people drawing closer. Recognizing my uninvited guests, I reached out.

[P100]
*Fwoosh.*

[P101]
A warm breeze swept through the room. Qi flowed from my palm and gently pushed the door open, revealing familiar faces.

[P102]
“What took you so long? I texted you ages ago.”

[P103]
“I’m sorry. I couldn’t be reached for a while.”

[P104]
I’d been about to lay into the latecomers, but I tilted my head.

[P105]
“Couldn’t be reached? Did you go into a Gate or something?”

[P106]
“Something like that.”

[P107]
“…Either you did or you didn’t. What’s ‘something like that’ supposed to mean?”

[P108]
“Butler Kim and I had somewhere to stop. It was important, so it couldn’t be helped.”

[P109]
Team Leader Choi stepped inside as he answered. Butler Kim followed, closed the door, and gave me a slight nod.

[P110]
*Haven’t seen him in a while.*

[P111]
Butler Kim had hardly shown his face at the Guild lately. What important business had the two of them been handling?

[P112]
It had been about a week since I’d seen him, and the question lingered. But something more urgent needed our attention. Team Leader Choi knew it too.

[P113]
“We can discuss that later. First, let’s look at the information Mr. Johnson gave you.”

[P114]
“Oh. Here.”

[P115]
I played the footage again. By the time they’d gone through every video and the attached materials, both their faces had hardened.

[P116]
“Worldwide magical power readings up seven percent?”

[P117]
Butler Kim’s usually gentle voice cracked. He turned to Team Leader Choi.

[P118]
“Young Master.”

[P119]
“Yes. It’s progressing faster than we expected. This is serious.”

[P120]
Seven percent wasn’t merely a rise. *Surge* was closer to the mark.

[P121]
And the effect of that surge was plain in the footage.

[P122]
“The monsters…”

[P123]
I nodded and finished Team Leader Choi’s thought.

[P124]
“Yeah. They’ve gotten fucking strong.”

[P125]
Rising magical power readings meant stronger monsters. The Giant Mantis in the first video had held its own even after taking a hit from Fire Rain.

[P126]
*It was like watching Chikorita get a tan from Charizard’s flames.*

[P127]
Type advantages were supposed to mean something. But as magical power readings climbed, the monsters were growing strong enough to shrug those advantages off.

[P128]
In a situation this fucked, places that kept their precious Hunters deployed in minimal numbers as a precaution were bound to be overwhelmed.

[P129]
To sum it up…

[P130]
“We’re fucked. It’s five minutes to a complete shitshow.”

[P131]
Things were moving at a ridiculous pace. Keep this up, and monsters might be part of the weather forecast by the end of the year.

[P132]
A pretty weathercaster would point to a map of the Korean Peninsula no bigger than a booger and explain it all:

[P133]
“Tomorrow, goblins are expected in Cheorwon, Gangwon Province, instead of heavy snow. They may pile up to twenty meters, so residents should grab their shields and antidotes and evacuate immediately.”

[P134]
“…”

[P135]
*Fuck. Heavy snow is annoying enough. Now monsterfall? Seriously?*

[P136]
Just imagining monsters pouring down from the sky made my heart shrivel.

[P137]
Of course, I wasn’t going to sit around twiddling my thumbs until then. I had to stop Korea from turning into Hell Peninsula, whatever it took.

[P138]
*I’d kept this possibility in mind, but… it’s definitely happening too fast.*

[P139]
I’d thought we had a little more time. The prospect of bringing forward *that thing*—the plan I’d been working on little by little since Murim—weighed on me.

[P140]
That was when Team Leader Choi spoke.

[P141]
“At this point, we can’t keep it hidden any longer.”

[P142]
He turned off the hologram. His voice was low.

[P143]
“It’s already beyond what can be concealed at a national level. The longer we wait to tell people, the worse the confusion will be.”

[P144]
This wasn’t a wave that would pass. It was a tsunami that might sweep whole cities away.

[P145]
I sighed. “What are you planning to do?”

[P146]
“Gate defenses come first right now. We need a breakwater before the tsunami hits.”

[P147]
“Strengthen the defenses?”

[P148]
“That will leave us with fewer Hunters for raids, and we won’t be able to make full use of all the Gates Peace Guild owns. But I know which matters more.”

[P149]
“That’s a relief.”

[P150]
I let out a quiet laugh. Team Leader Choi knew where to draw the line. He had grand ambitions of swallowing Ares Guild, but he also knew when to push forward and when to stop.

[P151]
*That’s the biggest difference between him and Lee Jungryong.*

[P152]
“Then we should focus on the Gates,” I said. “It’s a shame, but we’ll have to put Ares Guild on hold for a while…”

[P153]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P154]
“Yes?”

[P155]
Team Leader Choi’s clear eyes were fixed on me.

[P156]
“I said Gate defenses would be my top priority. I never said I would put Ares Guild on hold.”

[P157]
“…!”

[P158]
*What?*

[P159]
My eyes widened. Team Leader Choi went on.

[P160]
“I told you I had important business to take care of.”

[P161]
“Then that important business was…?”

[P162]
“A major figure in Ares Guild. A war hero who helped my maternal grandfather bring the Great Cataclysm to an end. Once the friend Lee Jungryong trusted most. And now the leader of the largest faction within Ares threatening Go Jun.”

[P163]
His voice was gentler than ever, with thorns hidden beneath it.

[P164]
“Everything crumbles from the inside.”

[P165]
[^1]: A pyeong is a Korean unit of area, about 35.6 square feet; this office is over 3,500 square feet.
[^2]: Patrache is the dog from the story commonly known in Korea as *A Dog of Flanders*.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
